text: On Frankfurt's hierarchical theory, an unwilling addict who takes the drug while sincerely willing at the higher order not to want it thereby exercises full free will.
explanation: This is false: the unwilling addict's effective first-order desire conflicts with the second-order volition he endorses, so his will is not one he can call his own, which is precisely a failure of free will on Frankfurt's account. Freedom requires that the will moving you be the one you endorse at the higher order.
